newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka to free Cuban-crewed ship.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka to free Cuban-crewed ship.

text.p: The Sri Lankan navy said on Tuesday it will soon free a Cyprus-registered freighter seized in waters off a Tamil rebel stronghold in the north of the island, saying it found no evidence of weapons on board.

The 1,674-tonne Caribbean Queen, with a crew of 28 Cubans, was seized by navy patrol boats on Sunday after it ignored repeated radio calls and warning shots from military aircraft and started manoeuvres to escape, the Defence Ministry said.
Separately, Tamil Tiger rebels attacked a remote police post earlier on Tuesday in the troubled north of the country, killing 15 policemen and guards, military and police officials said.

The incidents came a week into the government's biggest offensive this year against the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels, who are fighting for a separate homeland for minority Tamils in the north and east of the island.
"We searched the ship after she was detained because she was making suspicious movements," a navy spokesman told Reuters. "Nothing suspicious was found and we're going to release her."
The Caribbean Queen was stationary in Sri Lanka's territorial waters just off the coast of Mullaitivu, an LTTE stronghold, when it was seized.
It was taken to the government-held eastern port of Trincomalee, but its cargo hold was empty.
A Defence Ministry statement on Monday said the ship originally reported having engine trouble. The vessel was fired on and forced to stop when it suddenly started its engines and tried to sail away.
The ship's crew were not hurt in the incident. The vessel would be released after making repairs in Trincomalee, the navy said.
The navy spokesman said it was not clear how the crew explained the ship's actions during the incident.
Cuba's ambassador to Sri Lanka flew to Trincomalee but Cuban embassy officials in Colombo refused to comment on the case.

A Defence Ministry spokesman confirmed the LTTE attack on the remote police post in the village of Sungawila in Polonnaruwa district, 200 km (125 miles) northeast of Colombo, but could not immediately give details.
LTTE spokesmen were not available for comment.
At least 10 other police and local militia members were wounded in the attack early on Tuesday, the military and police officials in Colombo, who asked not to be named, said.
Defence Ministry spokesman Brigadier Tissa Jayatunga said there were two other attacks in the north on Monday.
He said the LTTE ambushed an army patrol in Puttur, in northern Jaffna peninsula, killing two soldiers. Three rebels were also killed, he said.
Also on Monday, navy boats and air force bombers sank a big rebel boat near an island in the narrow Palk Strait separating Sri Lanka and southern India, killing at least one rebel.

The army has been consolidating its positions after a 22 km (14 mile) thrust into rebel-held territory northwest of Vavuniya, a government stronghold 220 km (138 miles) north of Colombo, in its biggest offensive this year.
The offensive was launched on February 4.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war, now in its 14th year. The LTTE says the toll is much higher.
